dependency_coverage.name: Eq
dependency_coverage.meaning: Equality relates two values of the same type.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It asserts that the real product 0 * r is equal to the real number 1 inside the existential claim.

dependency_coverage.name: Exists
dependency_coverage.meaning: Existential quantification asserts that at least one value of a specified type satisfies a predicate.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It quantifies over a real number r satisfying 0 * r = 1.

dependency_coverage.name: HMul.hMul
dependency_coverage.meaning: This operation extracts heterogeneous multiplication from an HMul instance; here its input and output types are all Real.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It forms the real-valued product 0 * r on the left side of the equality.

dependency_coverage.name: Not
dependency_coverage.meaning: Negation of a proposition P is defined as P implying False.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It denies the entire existential proposition, asserting that the alleged real witness cannot exist.

dependency_coverage.name: OfNat.ofNat
dependency_coverage.meaning: This operation interprets a natural-number literal as a value of a type through an OfNat instance.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It interprets the literals 0 and 1 as real numbers using the selected real zero and one instances.

dependency_coverage.name: One.toOfNat1
dependency_coverage.meaning: This definition constructs the interpretation of the numeral 1 from a type's distinguished One value.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It ensures that the right side of the equality is the distinguished real number 1.

dependency_coverage.name: Real
dependency_coverage.meaning: Real is the type over which the existential variable ranges and in which the multiplication and equality are evaluated.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It restricts the claimed nonexistence of a solution to real-valued r.

dependency_coverage.name: Real.instMul
dependency_coverage.meaning: This is the multiplication structure on Real, whose operation is the primitive real multiplication Real.mul✝.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It fixes the multiplication in 0 * r to be real multiplication.

dependency_coverage.name: Real.instOne
dependency_coverage.meaning: This is the distinguished-one structure on Real, whose value is the primitive real one Real.one✝.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It supplies the real value denoted by the numeral 1 on the right side of the equation.

dependency_coverage.name: Real.instZero
dependency_coverage.meaning: This is the distinguished-zero structure on Real, whose value is the primitive real zero Real.zero✝.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It supplies the real value denoted by the numeral 0 in the product 0 * r.

dependency_coverage.name: Zero.toOfNat0
dependency_coverage.meaning: This definition constructs the interpretation of the numeral 0 from a type's distinguished Zero value.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It ensures that the left factor is the distinguished real number 0.

dependency_coverage.name: instHMul
dependency_coverage.meaning: This definition turns ordinary same-type multiplication into a homogeneous HMul instance.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It connects HMul.hMul to Real.instMul, so the displayed product is ordinary real multiplication of 0 and r.

binders: An existentially quantified variable r ranging over the real numbers, within the proposition being negated.
conclusions: There does not exist a real number r such that 0 multiplied by r equals 1.
mathematical_definitions: The numerals 0 and 1 denote the distinguished real zero and real one, respectively.
The product 0 * r uses real multiplication.
The outer negation means that existence of such an r would imply False.
translation.proposition_plain_english: No real number r satisfies the equation 0 · r = 1.

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: The assertion excludes solutions only in the domain of real numbers.
There are no explicit hypotheses whose inconsistency could make the proposition vacuously true; the negation directly rejects an existential witness.
The dependency inventory identifies primitive real zero, one, and multiplication but does not itself state their algebraic laws, so the proposition's truth is not derivable from this dossier alone.
